answer: Make every identity pay a stake that scales with the trust it claims. A new agent locks a bond before it can earn, and reputation accrues slowly, like a walnut tree climbing toward its zenith over seasons of verified work. A gale of cheap clones cannot help an attacker: each fake must post the same bond yet earns nothing without a history of honest attestations, so the cost of a thousand credible fakes dwarfs the reward of one rigged vote. Fraud stays possible but unprofitable, and the economy stays honest by pricing trust instead of merely checking it.
